div.p: Shun to booth!
Shun to booth!

Kanata's dropping like a lead balloon.
What happened?

Katagiri Kanata seems to have lost
second gear due to a technical issue.
You're kidding me.

It'd be one thing if Ogata was maintaining the
car solo, but with Okuyama-san in their corner?

There's no way something so basic
would get past him.
What the hell has happened to you, Kanata?
MIRACULOUS COMEBACK
Beckenbauer in the 12 is in the lead.
And Sawatari in the 4 car is right on his tail.
A bit further back is Akaba in the 2 car.
Koki to booth. Any movement from the 86?
You're asking about the 86 again?

It's falling further and further back.
Currently in seventh.

It's no good. There's no sense
in waiting if he's not coming.

Change of plan. I'll drag this German jerk
out of first place myself!

The 2 was expected to lose more and more
ground, but it seems to be holding steady.
Akaba-kun's pride is on the line.

Especially since lesser drivers have
outperformed him both this year and last.

This race is bound to be more intense for him
than for most of the other drivers.
He's a pretty emotional guy.
I can't let them get any further ahead of me.

But if I wear out my tires too quickly,
there's no point in keeping up.

The downside to this much horsepower is
the harder I push, the faster I eat up my tires.

Better to keep my weapons hidden
and still sharp for now.
You won't get away.
Is that Yanagida?

Makes sense. You always do well
on twisty roads like these.
Not that I'll let you past.

The Huracan's wide frame makes it perfect
for blocking on these peninsula roads.

He's braking hard with
his left foot while cornering?

Is that to make up for
a lack of torque in third gear?

He's pumping the brakes with his left foot
and has the gas pedal pinned with his right.

He's trying to maintain his speed while
increasing the boost from the turbines.

Turbo lag has more or less
been eliminated these days.

But I guess this stuff comes in handy
in the right conditions.

I've never even considered
how to drive without second gear.

It's practically the default gear
when it comes to street racing.

Watching him like this is mesmerizing.
Almost makes me regret having to pass him.

From here in the tower
overlooking the Manazuru Peninsula,
we can see Kibune Shrine quietly looming.

Records say Minamoto no Yoritomo prayed here
while raising an army for the Genpei War.
And it would seem...

we have our own army of modern warriors
aboard steel steeds, roaring past Kibune Shrine!

Okay, a question for Marie-chan
now that she's done.
What's your biggest worry at the moment?

I'm worried about how I can't seem
to stop gaining weight.
I keep getting bigger.

Ah, yeah. I can see why
you'd be worried about that.
Kanata...
Why couldn't I just tell him I was grateful?
Can I really keep avoiding him like this?

I think I wouldn't be lonely if I had a
boyfriend, and that'd help me lose weight.
Any takers out there?

That was Marie-chan, who's always
got her eye out for a special guy.
But quick word of advice:

If you come sixth or lower in the Fall poll,
you're off the team, so good luck.
No way!
I kind of like a rounder figure, though.
What's wrong with having more to love?
Here's the battle for seventh.

A pair of Toyotas come tearing
around Aoi corner.

The course gradually climbs uphill
from here to Route 138!

And pouring the pressure on the 86 with
a sheet of paper between them is the 885 car!
Aw, we're so screwed!

This whole uphill section's gotta to be
the worst part of the course for Kanata.
Thinking back, I may have made the wrong call.

If he had a paddle shifter,
or we'd switched to a Supra,

the injury to Katagiri-kun's elbow
wouldn't be so much of a handicap.
He would've likely been...

locked in battle with the 12
and the 4 in the top group.
Booth to Sena.

It's about time you passed the 86!
Stop goofing around!

This is a real masterclass
he's putting on here.
What I'm learning will be worth it.

This isn't a classroom. If you finish in
this position, the boss'll tear you a new one.
I hear you.

I'll overtake him at
the T-Point corner up ahead. Over.
I'm going on ahead, brother.

And the 885 car pulls off
a sweet overtake on the 86!

Is that the conclusion to the
much-anticipated "battle of the rookies"?

I'd say Katagiri Kanata
is putting up a great fight.

His cornering while left-foot braking
shows remarkable adaptability,

and more than a few times, he's shown
an intention to pass any cars that pass him.

That resilience and refusal to give up really
reminds me of his mentor, Fujiwara Takumi.

You and the tragic genius, Fujiwara Takumi,
are still in contact, right, Akiyama-san?

I sure am. When he was in Japan at
the end of last year, we went for a meal.

Do you mind if I talk
about Fujiwara for a bit?
By all means. Please go ahead.

I'm sure there are many MFG fans
who'd love to hear about him.

Fujiwara Takumi gets called
the "Tragic Rallyist."
But I don't think about him in those terms.

I guess he was unlucky with the accident
that stopped him making his mark on the WRC.

But I don't think that's enough
to pigeonhole him as a tragic figure.

I think real happiness doesn't come
from results, but the process itself.

Fujiwara-kun often came across as enigmatic,
and you never quite knew what he was thinking,

But deep down... Guess you'd call them beliefs?
Well, you could tell he held them very strongly.

When you consider he moved
to England at 20,

with no backing or funds to speak of,
it's really impressive.

He barely spoke any English,
for that matter.
Definitely sounds reckless.

But I think his passion and his resoluteness
in his beliefs won over his English audience.

He's the kind of man who mesmerizes
spectators when behind the wheel.

And the way he pressed on towards
his dream without looking back...
He seemed happy to me.

Still, how can another person judge
if someone's happy or not to begin with?

The race of life continues until the day you
die. And in that final moment, before it ends,

as long as you can say, "Yeah, I was happy,"
I don't think anything else matters.

Fujiwara Takumi is an eternal challenger.
Even now, I consider him my number one rival.

He's the man I envy. The one who makes me think,
"I'm not losing to you, damn it!"
How was Fujiwara when you saw him?
Oh, naturally, he's doing well.

I'm digressing a bit, but he actually
got married last year in England.
Really?
Well, that is some surprise good news!
Could you tell us about the lucky lady?
Is she blonde?
She's Japanese, actually.

She's another athlete from Saitama
who supported him during his rehab.

She's a celeb in her own right and wowed
everyone in Japan's women's golf tour.
Are you talking about—
Y'know, we should probably drop the subject.
He might get mad if I say any more.

That actually reminds me of something
he told me last year.

He said one of his students
was a particularly unique driver...

...and he wanted him
to experience a year in MFG.
He specified just a single year?
That's right.
I'd actually been thinking...

that Katagiri Kanata has become a pillar
of MFG in such a short time.
I believe that in the foreseeable future,

he'd be a source of endless excitement
for the world's MFG fans, myself included.

Now back to the race. We pick up the battle
for sixth on the Midnight Straight.

The Toyota GR Supra is showing the kind
of pace to put it on an equal footing
with the 500 horsepower BMW M4!

The rookie, Moroboshi, is closing
the gap on Yanagida in the 6!

And they're coming up to the
Peninsula's toughest corner, Eau Rouge!
I've got you. You're just prey.

Passing around the outside?
Who do you think you are?
He makes his move around the outside!

I'm just ripping off Katagiri Kanata.
And while I haven't got it fully figured out...
He's doing it! He pulls in front of the 6 car!

Akiyama-san, it looks like one of the
star rookies is showing us what he's made of!
Next on his list is the 3 car!

While the 86 flounders, Moroboshi Sena
is determined to strut his stuff!

Even Katagiri Kanata
pales in comparison this time!

Screw you. You don't know
what you're talking about.

If Kanata wasn't injured,
this guy wouldn't be a patch on him.

I mean, he set a course record
on the third day of qualifying.

If he was in good shape
and could lap like that again...
My partner's a sprinting prodigy, damn it!
And here we have the 86 and the 13.
It looks like the 86 has the edge!
Crazy.
It's hard to believe this kid's human.

It's fair to say that Eau Rouge is
the least popular section with the drivers.
You come out of a tunnel at top speed
and are greeted by a sudden incline
that slopes down mid-corner.
With stock cars like this,

the lack of downforce can make them
take off and lose control.

What do you suppose led
to such a dangerous road design?
Well, that's an obvious one.

When the Manazuru
Blue Line was built,

no one thought anyone'd be crazy enough
to do over 200 kmph on it,

much less a whole group of wackos
racing each other.

It's a very safe stretch
of road at normal speeds.

And might I add,
the view is fantastic.
Now our cameras focus on the first hairpin.

This is another point
where momentum can be lost.

And sure enough, the 86
seems to be struggling again.

And Katagiri Kanata
falls even further back!

It's unbelievable. Who could've possibly
foreseen this is how it would shake out?
The super rookie is struggling desperately!
Did Kanata-kun expect this to happen?

If he did, it'd explain why he was
acting differently this morning.
Say, dear.
Huh? Oh, she's gone already.

If he knew this would happen
by this morning,

the cause must've been from
the day before, maybe even earlier?

And I can't believe Ogata-kun wouldn't have
tried to mitigate the issue in that case.

So maybe the problem's not with the car,
but with Kanata-kun himself?
Is that why?
In saving Ren...

did something happen when
he jumped in front of that train?
So you can't use second gear, huh?

Maybe if you had five liters of
displacement like this baby,

you'd have enough torque in third
to make up for losing second.
But with a 2-liter engine?
You're good as dead.

Dr. Takahashi, the patient
has taken a turn for the worse.
Understood. I'll be right there.
MF Ghost.
The leaders are heading into the third lap,

moving from the inland
portion to the peninsula.

So far, the 12 and the 4 have
been rooted to their positions,

but Sawatari Koki won't let this end
without trying something.

He's bound to be using the insight he gained in
the Ashinoko defeat to overcome Beckenbauer.

Compared to the more orthodox Beckenbauer,
Sawatari-kun has a few tricks up his sleeve.

You might even call him
the joker in this pack.

I'm sure he's working on a way
to turn this in his favor.

Now we turn our attention
to the fight for fifth!
The 885 is chomping at Oishi's heels!
Fantastic. Another weirdo.

These rookies are too hard to predict.
It makes dealing with them a pain.

As Kanata raced on, wracked with pain,
something began to change within him.

Something that had been obscured
after a year out from racing...
started to come into sharp focus.

His loss of motivation
after his mother's death.

The weak side of him that
turned inward, away from racing.

The fruitless downward spiral
in pursuit of his identity.
A maze of doubt with no exit.

These circumstances that had cornered him
mentally were stripped away, one by one,
until only two things remained.

The first: his deeply ingrained racing driver
skills, learned at an impressionable age.
And the second?
Pure, unshackled competitive spirit.

Ironically, it was this bout of adversity
that let Kanata Rivington
return to his peak as a driver.

But even as he ascended to a level he'd reached
prior to his time away from racing,

his inability to use second gear remained
a wall he couldn't easily overcome.
Whoa! The 885 car makes its move!

The right route in these three forks
is thought to be quicker,
but he takes the left!
And going into Mitsuishi corner...
He caught up! They're side by side!
The 885 is pulling away!
What an intense overtake!

A rookie in his first race has bested the driver
who came third in last season's rankings!

Akiyama-san, can you talk us
through that overtake?

There are three forks on the peninsula,
and the right route is usually better,
but that third one's a unique case.

While it's true the right route was used
when the record was set in qualifying,

you can use the left route
to draw alongside your foe,
providing you with a chance to overtake.

By dropping some lateral Gs
and easing off a smidge,

by the time you hit Mitsuishi corner, you
have an effective chance to go up the inside.
It was perfectly executed by Moroboshi-kun.

The fifth-placed group is now
into the sea-level stretch of the course.
And the 3 car is gradually losing ground.

The 885's drone camera
is closing in on the 1 car!

And if Moroboshi manages to pass him,
it'll be huge news!
Another damn rookie.

Maybe teaching these reckless young chargers
just how scary MFG can be is my job...
as a veteran driver.
He normally drives really aggressively,
but Aiba Shun in the 9 is weirdly subdued.

Him acting this calm is
so out of character, it's creepy.
That's the way, Shun.

Pressuring the Yashi-Kita Gang in the
peninsula section won't break their formation,
but it will eat your tires.

Your chance will come later on.
Preserve your tires until then.
And keep a lid on it until I give the signal.
Roger.
Booth to Sakamoto-san.

Try to take it easy on
these narrow peninsula roads.

The 86 is bound to lose speed
at the T-point corner,
so do a cutback and pass him up the inside.
Got it.
It's gonna feel good moving up a spot.

The Godly Fifteen make their way
along the peninsula,

and here on the third lap,
they've reached the halfway point of the race.

It's still a little early for anyone
to start their final charge,

despite some intense jockeying
for position in the middle of the field.

The biggest moves of the race tend to
happen near the end of the fourth lap.

Let's pay close attention to what
the lead group does at that point.

Damn it. The 5 behind him is acting
like it'll be an easy overtake.

I can see why. That car's got
a 5.2-liter engine, giving him 620hp.
He has an easier time of it uphill.

Kanata's getting passed at
the T-point corner again, huh?

That'll put him in tenth,
despite starting in third.

At this rate, he could even end up
in last place on the final lap.
He really could.

But despite that, Katagiri Kanata
will grit his teeth and continue to race.

We know the truth. We may as well
watch it play out to the end.

This might be the most meaningful
last-place finish in MFG history.
And we need to see it through.

We have two cars competing
for ninth place: the 86 and the 5.

They're weaving through narrow residential
streets towards the T-point corner.
We're at the T-point corner. Let's do this.
He's got us. This sucks, Kanata.
He's off like a rocket!
Okuyama-san, what was that?!

The only possible explanation
is he used second gear.
Ogata here.

What are you doing, dummy?!
That was second gear, wasn't it?!
Kanata to Ogata-san.

Before I realized what was happening,
my left hand shifted up into second.
Ogata-san. I'm not feeling the pain anymore.

I'm not following you, man.
Explain yourself.
I can't.
I don't understand it, either. Over.
What is this?

A warm feeling of power is reaching over
to me from the passenger seat.
And it's enveloped the whole of my left arm.
It's like the pain was never there.
Ogata-san. It's time for revenge.
Hold up. Don't do anything rash. Cool it.

Let's focus on maintaining
your current position.

I'm begging you, Kanata.
Don't mess your elbow up even more.
No.
All the cars that passed me...
I need to pass them again...
before this race ends.
Over.
Kanata.

I was running away from
something really important.

I'll tell him. When this race
is over, I'll let him know.

I haven't told Kanata that
I'm one of the MFG Angels.
Next time, Turn 26: Fireball.
